goal: Extend Task Managers (Basecamp) so the owner can create lists and to-dos, update to-dos, read full descriptions, associate lists with a repo and directory, see and filter open items, and dispatch an attachable interactive agent on an item. Feature logic and state live in the Arc service (services/harness-audit) as event-sourced aggregates; the Python CLI stays a thin provider driver.
constraints: Python modules use the standard library only; no new Rust dependency.
Task-manager text is untrusted: fenced for agents, never in file names, branch names, commit messages, pull requests or event payloads.
Free text reaches the CLI through a file path, never an argument.
A write is one request, never repeated after a failure except once after a 401 and a successful refresh; forget the project cache after any write.
Ids are validated before anything runs; requests go only to configured provider hosts without following redirects.
Every /tasks route passes host check, owner gate, Origin check and CSRF in the documented order.
Only repositories named in repos of task-managers.json may receive an agent or a run.
No Arc projectors are registered; index tables are created on open and caught up from events.
A dispatched agent's first headless turn is read-only; edits only after attach.
Work on master in the main checkout; no commits unless the user asks.

non_goals.description: The gated pipeline stays as it is.
Leave the unrelated uncommitted audit changes alone (styles.css, turn-context.html, reports.rs, ui.rs, workflow.rs, tasks/turn-context-json.json).
No new providers besides Basecamp; the seed packet keeps its current bounds; no Rust HTTP client.

acceptance.criterion: list-create, todo-create and todo-update each send exactly one write, an update keeps untouched fields, a failed write is not repeated, the project cache is dropped; get --full returns a long description whole

command: sh tests/task-managers.sh && sh tests/task-managers-write.sh && sh tests/task-managers-seed.sh && sh tests/task-managers-runs.sh && sh tests/task-managers-auth.sh

acceptance.criterion: Service tests pass: associations (unknown repo refused, survives restart, removal restores config default), open-item filters (AND, no done items, default preset), agents (start records session and code, attach --print gives the exact resume command, done opens one draft PR and removes the worktree, second start refused), and every new /tasks route (gate order, id validation, argv)
docs/task-managers.md covers the new commands, exits, routes, state and security notes; AGENTS.md maps the new modules
